league_run.design: all 90 ordered matchups x 200 games, every game with its own seed
league_run.event_rates_sampled_vs_engine_input: all eight outcomes within 0.1 percentage point of the matchup probabilities the engine sampled from
league_run.team_runs_histogram_peak: 2-3 runs; maximum 24 runs in one team-game; maximum 113 plate appearances in one game

team_strength.note: Simulated win percentages span about 44-54% against 36-65% in reality: the engine uses each team's starter for the whole game and its regular nine, so bullpen and bench depth are absent

findings.issue: Seed choice in batch runs biased the results
findings.detail: Park-Miller's first draw is (seed + 1) * 16807 / (2^31 - 1). Consecutive small seeds (1, 2, 3, ...) all opened with a strikeout draw (+1.7 percentage points of strikeouts). Seeds drawn from a Park-Miller stream are states of that stream, so games became shifted copies of one sequence (runs 6.5 per team-game). Reusing one seed list across matchups shrank the effective sample to the list length.
findings.fix: spreadSeeds draws distinct seeds with dart:math Random, the same way the app picks seeds (Random().nextInt), and each game in a batch gets its own seed. The app was never affected: it picks a uniform random seed per game.
findings.evidence: after the fix every sampled event rate matches the engine input; regression test 'spreadSeeds' and the 1,000-game z-score test

findings.issue: Run scoring about 19% below the real league (engine 2.0.0: 4.16 vs 5.07)

decomposition.reading: With league-average plate appearances the engine still scores about 10% less (omitted steals, errors, wild pitches, balks). Regular nine against a starter for the whole game costs another 5-6%: starters strike out more and walk fewer batters than the league as a whole (strikeouts 20.3% vs 19.5%, walks 8.4% vs 9.4%).

findings.decision: Approved by the user on 2026-11-25: add only advancement on outs, with realistic mid-grid rates, and document the rest instead of fitting new events.
findings.change: Engine 2.1.0: on an other out with fewer than two outs (not a double play), the runner on second takes an open third with probability 0.35 and the runner on first takes an open second with probability 0.20. The play is logged as runner_advanced_on_out and shown as '진루타'.
findings.sensitivity: runs per team-game range only from 4.20 to 4.32 across 2B->3B 0.25-0.45 and 1B->2B 0.10-0.30 (week5_calibration_report.json), so the choice is not a fit to the real total

limitations: Run scoring remains about 17% below the real league (4.21 vs 5.07) because steals, errors, wild pitches and bullpen use are not modeled
Tie rate is higher than reality (3.5% vs 2.4%), a consequence of lower scoring
No home advantage is modeled (home win percentage 50.4%)
Team strength is compressed relative to real standings; the game is a virtual matchup of each team's regulars and starter, not a forecast
Advancement-on-out rates are approximations; the dataset has no KBO totals for runners advancing on outs to fit them against
